title: 第 37 課｜非對稱陀螺：橢球與球面交出的路徑｜Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學
description:
把歐拉方程用到最複雜的情形：三個主慣量都不相同的自由非對稱陀螺，並約定 I₃ 大於 I₂ 大於 I₁。這時已經有兩個守恆量：能量與角動量的大小。用角動量的分量寫出來，能量守恆給出橢球面 M₁²/I₁ + M₂²/I₂ + M₃²/I₃ = 2E，三個半軸是 √(2E I₁)、√(2E I₂)、√(2E I₃)；角動量守恆給出球面 M₁² + M₂² + M₃² = M²。所以 M 的尖端必須同時待在橢球面與球面上，也就是走在兩者的交線上；交線存在的條件是 2E I₁ 小於 M² 小於 2E I₃，也就是球半徑落在橢球最短與最長的半軸之間。固定能量而改變 M，這族交線的變化很有意思：M 最小時是繞 x₁ 的兩個小圈，M 變大時圈也變大；在 M² = 2E I₂ 時它們退化成兩條通過 x₂ 的平面曲線（其實就是球面上的兩個大圓）；再大下去則變成繞 x₃ 的兩個小圈。由於路徑都是閉曲線，M 相對於物體的運動是週期的，一個週期內掃出一個錐面。更重要的是靠近各軸的路徑性質不同：靠近 x₁ 與 x₃ 的路徑整條都待在該軸附近，經過 x₂ 的路徑卻會跑到很遠的地方——這就是繞最小與最大主軸的轉動穩定、繞中間主軸不穩定的原因。要求時間相依性，就用兩個守恆律把 Ω₁ 與 Ω₃ 用 Ω₂ 表示，代進第二條歐拉方程，得到一條一階方程；積分後是橢圓積分，換成無因次變數並定義模數 k² 之後化為標準形式，反解得到雅可比橢圓函數，於是 Ω₁ 正比於 cn τ、Ω₂ 正比於 sn τ、Ω₃ 正比於 dn τ，週期由第一類完全橢圓積分 K 決定。當兩個主慣量趨於相等時 k² 趨近於零，這三個函數退化成餘弦、正弦與常數，回到第 36 課的對稱陀螺。影片中所有的路徑都是把無力矩方程數值積分出來的真實軌跡。

本影片為《Landau–Lifshitz 經典力學》教學系列第 37 課（繁體中文版）。

title: Lesson 37 | The Asymmetrical Top: Paths Cut by an Ellipsoid and a Sphere | Landau–Lifshitz
description:
Euler's equations are applied to the hardest case: a free asymmetrical top with all three principal moments different, ordered so that I₃ is greater than I₂ is greater than I₁. Two integrals are already available, the energy and the magnitude of the angular momentum. Written in the components of M, energy conservation gives the ellipsoid M₁²/I₁ + M₂²/I₂ + M₃²/I₃ = 2E, with semiaxes √(2E I₁), √(2E I₂) and √(2E I₃), while conservation of M gives the sphere M₁² + M₂² + M₃² = M². The tip of M must therefore lie on both surfaces at once, so it travels along their curve of intersection, which exists only when 2E I₁ is smaller than M² and M² is smaller than 2E I₃, that is, when the radius of the sphere falls between the shortest and longest semiaxes. Holding the energy fixed and varying M sweeps out a whole family of these curves: for the smallest M they are two little loops about x₁, widening as M grows; at M² = 2E I₂ they degenerate into two plane curves through x₂, which are in fact two great circles of the sphere; beyond that they become loops about x₃. Since the paths are closed, the motion of M relative to the body is periodic, sweeping out a conical surface in one period. More importantly, the paths near the three axes behave differently: those near x₁ and x₃ stay entirely close to them, while the ones through x₂ run far away, which is why rotation about the least and greatest axes is stable and rotation about the middle axis is not. For the time dependence, the two conservation laws express Ω₁ and Ω₃ through Ω₂; substituting into the second Euler equation leaves a first-order equation whose integral is elliptic. In dimensionless variables with a modulus k² the integral takes standard form, and inverting it gives Jacobian elliptic functions: Ω₁ proportional to cn τ, Ω₂ to sn τ and Ω₃ to dn τ, with the period fixed by the complete elliptic integral K. As two moments approach each other k² tends to zero and the functions degenerate into cosine, sine and a constant, returning to the symmetrical top of lesson 36. Every path shown is a real trajectory, obtained by integrating the torque-free equations numerically.

Lesson 37 of the Landau–Lifshitz Classical Mechanics teaching series (English edition).
